notes.text: DDT RING FINALE is a lottery on e+, so enter now: one application for all 8. If you lose the draw, skip it and spend the morning in Kōenji instead.
First thing, the big suitcases go to Yamato for Haneda T3. Keep out everything you need until the flight, and save the waybills on a phone.
Bring cash for the Golden Gai seat charges and the Kōenji izakaya, and passports for tax-free and the bars. Thermae-yu turns away anyone with tattoos.

stops.summary: Ship the suitcases to Haneda now, and the last two days are bag-free until airline bag drop.
stops.story: Yamato will take your suitcases to Haneda T3, where you collect them on Tuesday. Until then you carry nothing heavier than a tote.
how: Hand the suitcases in at the Garfield House front desk or the nearest konbini; ask for airport delivery to Haneda T3.
Screenshot every waybill.
tips: Keep tax-free purchases and passports on you, not in the suitcase: you finish the paperwork at the Haneda T3 customs kiosk before bag drop.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: Hangover breakfast: seafood bowls and grill-your-own scallops at a 24-hour fish izakaya. Eat fast, the bell's at 11:30.
stops.story: Isomaru Suisan never shuts: you grill scallops, crab-miso shells and squid yourself on a tabletop grill. Last night it was the after-party for half of Shinjuku; this morning it's kaisen-don for eight wrecked people. It's on four floors, so a table for 8 is easy off-peak.
how: Walk 13 min from Garfield House to Shinjuku 3-chōme.
Order kaisen-don and a round of scallops for the grill.
Leave by 10:35: Marunouchi line to Yotsuya, then the JR Sōbu local to Suidobashi, 10:45→10:51 (¥380).
tips: Skip the highballs: you have a wrestling show to get through.
Course menus need booking the day before. The bowls don't.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: DDT's last show of the year at Korakuen Hall: comedy, stunts and title fights in wrestling's holy land. Lottery: apply now.
stops.story: DDT is Tokyo's most unhinged wrestling company: comedy spots, ladder stunts and serious title matches on the same card. Korakuen Hall is a sweaty 1,800-seat box where every seat is close to the ring. This is DDT's last show of the year, so expect them to go all out.
how: Apply on e+ now: it's a lottery (抽選), one application for all 8.
Doors 10:30, bell 11:30; you're out about 14:30.
After the show, take the yellow JR Chūō-Sōbu local from Suidobashi to Kōenji (¥260): weekend rapids skip Kōenji.
tips: One application for 8 usually gets a block of seats together. The south balcony is the cheap, rowdy part.
Lost the lottery? Skip it and go to Kōenji from late morning. Sareee-ISM, Mon 28 Dec 11:30 at the same hall, is first-come on e+.
The B.LEAGUE games (Kawasaki vs Chiba 15:05) are only a backup until bleague.jp confirms them.
stops.booking: Lottery on e+, apply now for 8 in one application
wishes: Pro wrestling: Pro Wrestling NOAH Thanksgiving 2026 at Korakuen Hall (Plan C had Fri 18 Dec)
Be bold: prefer one-of-a-kind, local-run, hard-to-book and group-scale things, and name a safe fallback beside every hard-to-book thing

stops.summary: Day-drinking under the JR tracks: cheap yakitori and highballs while the Chūō line rattles overhead.
stops.story: Kōenji is a scruffy, music-mad neighbourhood where Sunday afternoon drinking is normal. The izakaya under the tracks are smoky and tiny, and the trains rumble right over the plastic stools. Plan C's pick was Bariki, right under the tracks.
how: Find the izakaya under the JR tracks by Kōenji station.
Order yakitori and highballs, then a second round.
Then walk 3 min to the arcades.
tips: It's dark by the time you come out. In December that comes early.
Keep it to two rounds; the racks are waiting.
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly

stops.summary: Tokyo's grittiest vintage digging: punk, archive and bargain racks, cheaper and rougher than Shimokita.
stops.story: Locals and recent Xiaohongshu guides now send vintage hunters to Kōenji over Shimokitazawa. There are more shops and fewer tourists, and the racks are less curated and cheaper. Pal and Look arcades run south for blocks, and Kita-Kore Building on the north side is a warren of punk and designer-archive shops.
how: Split into 2–3 crews; the shops are tiny.
Hit Kita-Kore first (north of the tracks), then work south down Pal into Look arcade.
Regroup at 18:45 at the south end and take the Marunouchi line from Shin-Kōenji to Nishi-Shinjuku, 19:02→19:09 (¥180).
tips: Kita-Kore is listed 11:00–18:00, earlier than the arcades, which close about 20:00 on Sundays.
Pieces run ¥2,000–8,000; dig the ¥500–1,000 bargain racks.
If a shop does tax-free, you need ¥5,000 or more in that shop and a passport.
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls

stops.summary: Tokyo from 202 m for free, and the last good night for it before the year-end closure.
stops.story: The city government lets you up its tower for free, and from up there Tokyo's lights run out to the horizon. Down on the plaza, the building's facade turns into a huge projection-mapping screen after dark. The north deck closes tomorrow and both decks close on the 29th, so tonight is the night.
how: Walk-in only, no group bookings: expect a 20-30 minute queue at the lifts.
Go up first, then watch the projection show from outside.
Then take the Oedo line from Tochōmae to Shinjuku-nishiguchi, 20:30→20:32 (¥180).
tips: The north deck is listed only to 17:00, so at night it's probably the south one.
It can close suddenly in bad weather; check the tocho_tenbou X account.
Last entry 21:30.
wishes: Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes

stops.summary: Neon food hall with DJs: one big table, everyone eats a different region, the stage gets loud.
stops.story: Kabuki Yokocho is a noisy, neon food hall on the 2nd floor of Tokyu Kabukicho Tower, with regional stalls around a stage. You grab a long table, scatter to the gyoza, yakitori, seafood and Korean stalls, and reconvene with trays. DJs and karaoke battles keep it loud late.
how: Walk to Tokyu Kabukicho Tower and go up to the 2nd floor.
Claim a big shared table first, then split up and order at the stalls.
Then it's a 7-minute walk to Thermae-yu.
tips: Go easy on the drinks: the bath is next.
Skip Umi no Ie's ¥1,480 nomihodai. They refuse anyone under 20.
stops.booking: No booking needed; group bookings accepted
stops.hours: Open every day; listed 6:00–05:00, hours per stall
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly
Everyone stays together; every booking is for 8 at the same table or private room (8名で、同じテーブル/個室)

stops.summary: A natural hot-spring soak and sauna in the middle of Kabukichō: steam out the wrestling, the trains and the cold.
stops.story: Thermae-yu is a 24-hour natural hot-spring super-sento in the middle of Kabukichō. There are outdoor baths, saunas, and a lounge that sells beer. After a cold day of crate-digging it's the warmest place in Shinjuku.
how: Baths are separate by gender; meet back in the shared lounge.
Do the outdoor bath, then the sauna.
Be out well before 1:00.
tips: No tattoos: anyone with ink can't go in.
The weekend rate is higher, and staying between 1:00 and 6:00 costs extra.
Golden Gai is a 1-minute walk away.
wishes: A 24-hour onsen night (Thermae-yu in Kabukichō or Spa World in Shinsekai)

stops.summary: Two crews of 4, six alleys of tiny bars: hop the ones with English prices, then stagger home.
stops.story: Golden Gai is about 200 micro-bars across six alleys, most of them seating 6–8 people. You won't find a better bar crawl in Tokyo. Sunday night is calmer, so you have a better shot at getting in.
how: Split into two groups of 4 and hop neighbouring bars.
Pick bars that post English prices outside.
Pay the seat charge, have a drink, move on.
tips: Cash only, mostly: seat charges ¥500–1,500 and drinks about ¥700–1,000.
Walk past anything marked 'regulars only'.
Bring passports; the drinking age is 20.
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly
